findings.mechanism: The focus road anchors moral deviation; actual wider disappearance and orientation scenes keep the separate root branches concrete. Their contact makes the danger of straying include visibility, locatability, and effective guidance without collapsing them into one dictionary meaning.
findings.reader_payoff: The prayer seeks a direction that preserves a person's place within a supported course.
findings.containment: 32:10 voices a question about disappearance into earth, not an accepted claim that God cannot recover the lost. A stray's unknown owner is a human practical condition; 11:56 keeps every creature under divine control.

epistemic.reason: The supplied Arabic establishes the contact; the return to the focus is a bounded contextual interpretation rather than a replacement gloss.

findings.title: Different grammatical agencies do not settle causation
findings.claim: The focus directly addresses the giver of favor, leaves the agent of anger unspoken, and names the straying through an active participle. Wider passages explicitly name God as the agent of anger and of misguidance, so this asymmetry cannot establish a complete division of causal agency.
findings.mechanism: The focus's stated bestower and passive recipient contrast with the explicit 'God became angry with them' of 48:6; the active straying category meets divine misguidance in 7:186 and personally consequential deviation in 17:15. The different formulations foreground different relations without resolving their causal interaction.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can notice the grammatical asymmetry without deriving a doctrine of causation from an omitted agent.
findings.containment: The local passive still leaves its agent unspoken. Wider naming provides contextual attribution, not a syntactic insertion; divine and personal agency claims coexist without adjudication.

epistemic.reason: The supplied Arabic establishes the contact; the return to the focus is a bounded contextual interpretation rather than a replacement gloss.
